There are no imaging features to suggest an IDH-wildtype tumor, which typically presents in older patients with ring enhancement and necrosis.

This sign is highly specific for astrocytic lineage tumors (1p/19q non-codeleted) and is rarely, if ever, seen in oligodendrogliomas (1p/19q codeleted). While the frontal lobe location is common in oligodendrogliomas, it is not specific and is also a frequent site for astrocytomas. The overwhelming evidence from the T2-FLAIR mismatch sign points to a non-codeleted status.

overall_comment: The imaging findings in this young patient are highly characteristic of a low-grade, IDH-mutant astrocytoma. The presence of a T2-FLAIR mismatch sign is a very strong predictor of both IDH-mutant and 1p/19q non-codeleted status. The near-total lack of enhancement and absence of necrosis strongly support a CNS WHO grade 2 designation. The confidence in the molecular predictions is very high, while the confidence in grade is slightly lower as imaging cannot definitively rule out microscopic foci of anaplasia.
